messages.subject: Importing from text file of unknown origin
parts:
One of the apps that i am developing reads data from a text file that the user provides. The text file originates from a commercial software that runs under windows. The files seems to be in different encoding depending on the set-up of the user (users woldwide).  
And they have special characters included in some of the lines that i need to retrieve. I have attached a minimal example. There are two files attached (one that i made locally and one made on a windows PC). I can read the local but not the windows file.

Can you help?

ui.R:
shinyUI(fluidPage(
 textOutput("renderedtext")
        
))

server.R:
#special<-readLines("special_characters.txt")
special<-readLines("special_characters_WIN.txt")
shinyServer(function(input, output, session){
  output$renderedtext<-renderText(paste0("The special characters are ",special,"."))
  })

BTW: thanks for developing this amazing platform

Mette

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Importing from text file of unknown origin
parts:
You'd better not set the locale to C (is there a reason for that?).
renderText() uses capture.output(), which can destroy characters if
the locale is inappropriate, especially on Windows. One workaround is
to simply use a reactive, e.g.

output$renderedtext <- reactive({

paste0("The special characters are ",special,".")
})

Then as long as `special` was read with the correct encoding, the
characters should be displayed correctly.

BTW, it seems your special_characters_WIN.txt was also encoded in UTF8.

Regards,
Yihui
